title: reader config: drain_timeout_secs doc comment 'Set to 0 to exit immediately' is misleading
description: In crates/reader/src/config.rs, LimitsConfig::drain_timeout_secs has a doc comment that says 'Set to 0 to exit immediately.' This is inaccurate in two ways: (1) The field is Option<u64>, so None (field absent) and Some(0) are distinct states. None produces the 30-second default; Some(0) passes a zero-duration timeout to tokio::time::timeout. The doc does not explain this distinction. (2) Zero-duration behavior relies on tokio implementation details: a zero Duration fires immediately if the wrapped future is not immediately ready. This is not guaranteed by any public API contract. The doc should either remove the zero-value hint or replace it with an accurate description of what None vs. Some(0) do. The transit config's equivalent field omits the zero-value hint entirely, creating an asymmetry between the two configs governing the same concept.
